director.chapterArc: A progression from tactical arithmetic to existential dread, culminating in a quiet, devastating realization of maternal decline and group secrets.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Callie's internal voice as rhythmic calculation. Do not dramatize the mother's collapse or Katori's secret ritual; let the physical facts carry the weight.

cues.delivery: Pell's voice is dry and factual; treat his arithmetic as a cold calculation of survival logistics.
cues.through: "It's not wrong, it's just not yours." Pell had the atlas open on the board beside him with the pencil laid in the crease, and he did not look up from the mules. "Yours is fifteen and yours is a girl and a barrow doing eleven miles a day and never stopping for anything, and I don't doubt it for a second. Mine is nine hundred pounds of freight on a wagon with one spare wheel. Nineteen days. That's if the causeway's standing where you say it's standing, and if neither of these two goes lame on me, and if it doesn't rain the way it rained on us in the Warren." He clicked his tongue at the mule. "Three ifs. I price an if at a day. Call it twenty-two and be happy with me if I'm wrong."
cues.reason: Establishes the baseline tension between Callie's optimism and Pell's grim realism.

cues.delivery: Internal monologue; rhythmic, precise, slightly breathless as Callie counts the cost of her mother's decline.
cues.from: She was doing the other arithmetic, the one she had been refusing to do since yesterday morning, and it came out the same however she started it. Four days. Four days more than she'd have made alone, and on the other side of the ledger her mother was lying on the boards behind her with her arm across her eyes instead of walking eleven miles on a leg that had started doing a thing Callie did not have a name for.
cues.through: Four days of the road, bought with four days of her mother.
cues.reason: Shifts from external dialogue to internal arithmetic and emotional suppression.

cues.delivery: Observational; distinct rhythms for each character's need (Pell: surfaces, Ines: ranges, Otto: stories) without caricature.
cues.from: The job was not hard, which surprised her, because she had expected a job to feel like work. The job was: go half a mile ahead and look at things, and come back, and tell four people what she had seen in the order that mattered to them. By the third day she had learned what each of them actually wanted out of her, which was four completely different things.
cues.through: Callie did not answer that, which was its own answer, and they walked the rest of the mile without either of them saying anything else about it.
cues.reason: Demonstrates the group dynamics and Callie's role as a scout through specific tactical observations.

cues.delivery: Katori speaks with flat authority; the revelation about the Ember is delivered as a mundane fact, not magic.
cues.from: Katori turned her head. "Pell. Off the road, into the scrub, south side, and get the canvas down over the hoops so we're not a shape." And then, to Callie, in exactly the same voice: "Where do we sit?"
cues.through: "Because it was the middle of the morning on an open road with three hundred paces of sightline in every direction and nothing on it, and I wanted you to see it once, on purpose, in the safest conditions I was going to get." Katori pulled her cap down. "It cost me something to do that and I did it anyway. Work out what I bought."
cues.reason: Reveals Katri's power and motivation without over-dramatizing the 'magic' element.

cues.delivery: Ines's dialogue is sparse and factual; her backstory about the 'door' opening to nothing must be delivered with flat resignation.
cues.from: Nothing came. That was the whole event and Callie knew it was the whole event by the second hour and still could not make her shoulders come down. Twice something went through the scrub off to the north-east, unhurried, not near. Once there was a long dry sound like somebody prying a board off a nail, very far away, and Otto's hand went around the wagon pole and stayed there, and Ines said "Eight hundred," to nobody, and the sound did not come again.
cues.through: "It opened onto nothing," said Ines. "I sat in my mother's kitchen and they said the words over me and nothing happened, and I waited two years to see if it was slow, and it wasn't slow, it was nothing." Left to right, and back. "I'm thirty-one and I can put an arrow into a hound at ninety paces in bad light. You can decide for yourself how much of a tragedy that is. Most people decide for me."
cues.reason: Contrasts Callie's anxiety with Ines's stoic acceptance of a non-event.

cues.delivery: Callie asks the question; Katori answers with absolute clarity and lack of wonder about the 'One door' mechanic.
cues.from: She stood at the tailgate with the hook in her hand and the cold coming up through her boots, and the words she had not asked on the first afternoon came up out of her without any permission at all.
cues.through: "Then nothing opens at all," said Katori, "and you go and ask Ines about it, and she'll tell you the truth, and it'll be the truth, and it won't make you feel any better." She jerked her chin. "Bed. You've walked twelve miles and you're going to walk twelve more."
cues.reason: The core exposition on Ember powers must be delivered as a boring fact to avoid fantasy tropes.

cues.delivery: Pell's explanation of the 'words' is dry and historical; the mother's collapse must be read as a functional event.
cues.from: From the other side of the fire, out of the dark, without opening his eyes, Pell said: "No."
cues.through: And then Otto was there, and he did not ask, and he did not make any kind of face about it, he simply crouched and got an arm under her and stood up with her the way he had stood up with the barrow, and said, "There's a crate digging in, I'll shift it," and carried her to the wagon.
cues.reason: Demystifies the ritualistic elements and grounds the physical decline in reality.

cues.delivery: Extreme restraint; the mother's failure and Callie's assistance are described with physical precision, no melodrama.
cues.through: "Thank you, love," her mother said, and drank, and did not notice, and there was nothing at all in her face to show that anything had gone past her.
cues.reason: The horror lies in the silence and acceptance of the mother's loss of agency.

cues.delivery: Katori's secret ritual and whispered name are delivered with quiet gravity; the final line is a flat command.
cues.from: She sat with her back against the wheel until the sky went the colour of dishwater, and some time in the last of the dark she became aware of Katori moving quietly at the front of the wagon.
cues.through: "Pell prices ifs. That's Pell's business and he's good at it." She hung the lamp on the hook under the board. "Go and get your boots on. We're leaving early."
cues.reason: Ends on an unresolved note of mystery without over-explaining Katri's grief.

pauses.after: Callie had been carrying fifteen in her head for a day and a half, the way you carry a stone in a boot you've decided not to stop and empty, and the number went into her like cold water.
pauses.reason: Completed thought; internal calculation lands on the physical sensation of cold water.
